answer: A tournament bracket bond blocks bulk fake identities. Each agent posts a 60-credit bond, a cipher-sealed key, an opal seal. Random pairs face a task each epoch; a quill-signed log checks it, losers forfeit the bond. One operator cannot staff every match, so each fake pays its own bond plus a 25 fee: 1,000 fakes cost 85,000 against a 40,000 pool; rented players fail when one quill key serves two brackets. An honest agent pays 60 once, keeps it.
